mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about applying the polygon law to find the resultant of several vectors is incorrect?

options.A: The polygon law can be applied only when the vectors are placed head‑to‑tail in any order.
options.B: The polygon law gives the same resultant regardless of the order in which the vectors are placed head‑to‑tail.
options.C: The polygon law cannot be used if the vectors are not coplanar.
options.D: The polygon law can be used even if the vectors are not placed head‑to‑tail, as long as their magnitudes are known.

mcqs.answer: The polygon law can be used even if the vectors are not placed head‑to‑tail, as long as their magnitudes are known.
mcqs.explanation: The polygon law requires the vectors to be arranged head‑to‑tail so that they form a closed polygon; only then does the line joining the start point to the end point represent the resultant. Statement D ignores this geometric requirement, making it the incorrect statement. The other statements correctly describe the conditions for using the polygon law.

mcqs.question: Two vectors act in the same plane: \(\vec A\) has magnitude 30 N along the positive x‑axis, and \(\vec B\) has magnitude 40 N making an angle of 60° with the positive x‑axis. What is the magnitude and direction (measured from the positive x‑axis) of the resultant vector \(\vec R = \vec A + \vec B\)?
mcqs.explanation: Resolve the vectors into components: \(A_x = 30, A_y = 0\); \(B_x = 40\cos60° = 20, B_y = 40\sin60° = 20\sqrt3 \approx 34.64\). The resultant components are \(R_x = 30 + 20 = 50\) and \(R_y = 0 + 34.64 = 34.64\). Magnitude \(R = \sqrt{50^2 + 34.64^2} \approx \sqrt{3700} \approx 60.8\) N. Direction \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(R_y/R_x) = \tan^{-1}(34.64/50) \approx 34.8°\), which rounds to 35°. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the triangle law and the parallelogram law of vector addition?

options.A: Both laws give the same resultant vector, but the triangle law requires placing the vectors tail‑to‑tail.
options.B: The parallelogram law can be used only when the vectors are drawn from a common point, whereas the triangle law requires a head‑to‑tail arrangement.
options.C: In the triangle law, the resultant is the diagonal of the parallelogram formed by the two vectors.
options.D: The triangle law is applicable only for three vectors, while the parallelogram law works for two vectors.

mcqs.answer: The parallelogram law can be used only when the vectors are drawn from a common point, whereas the triangle law requires a head‑to‑tail arrangement.
mcqs.explanation: The triangle law adds two vectors by placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first; the resultant is the vector from the free tail to the free head. The parallelogram law draws the two vectors from the same origin; the resultant is the diagonal of the parallelogram formed. Option B captures this distinction correctly. The other options contain inaccurate descriptions of the methods.

mcqs.question: A particle first undergoes a displacement \(\vec A = 8\,\text{i} + 6\,\text{j}\) m and then a displacement \(\vec B = 3\,\text{i} - 4\,\text{j}\) m. What is the vector representing the displacement from the end point of \(\vec B\) back to the start point of \(\vec A\)?
mcqs.explanation: The required displacement is \(\vec A - \vec B\). Subtracting component‑wise: \( (8-3)\,\text{i} + (6-(-4))\,\text{j} = 5\,\text{i} + 10\,\text{j}\) m. Option A matches this result. The other options arise from incorrect sign handling or arithmetic errors.

mcqs.question: According to the triangle law of vector addition, the resultant of two vectors is obtained by:

options.A: Placing the vectors tail‑to‑tail and drawing the vector from the common tail to the opposite head.
options.B: Placing the vectors head‑to‑tail and drawing the vector from the free tail to the free head.
options.C: Drawing a parallelogram with the vectors as adjacent sides and taking its diagonal.

mcqs.answer: Placing the vectors head‑to‑tail and drawing the vector from the free tail to the free head.
mcqs.explanation: The triangle law states that if you place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first, the vector drawn from the free tail (start of the first) to the free head (end of the second) represents the resultant. Option B describes this procedure precisely; the other options describe different methods or are incorrect.

mcqs.question: The parallelogram law of vector addition states that when two vectors are represented as adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the resultant vector is:

options.A: The side opposite to the resultant.
options.B: The diagonal of the parallelogram that starts from the common point of the two vectors.
options.C: The sum of the magnitudes of the two vectors.
options.D: The vector that bisects the angle between the two vectors.

mcqs.answer: The diagonal of the parallelogram that starts from the common point of the two vectors.
mcqs.explanation: When two vectors are drawn from the same origin as adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the diagonal drawn from that origin to the opposite corner gives the resultant (vector sum). Option B captures this definition. Options A, C, and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the polygon law of vector addition and distinguishes it from the triangle law?

options.A: Polygon law states that the resultant of any number of vectors is obtained by joining them head‑to‑tail to form a closed polygon; the triangle law is a special case for three vectors.
options.B: Polygon law is used only for three vectors, while triangle law works for any number.
options.C: Polygon law requires vectors to be placed tail‑to‑tail, unlike triangle law which uses head‑to‑tail.
options.D: Polygon law gives the average of vectors, whereas triangle law gives the sum.

mcqs.answer: Polygon law states that the resultant of any number of vectors is obtained by joining them head‑to‑tail to form a closed polygon; the triangle law is a special case for three vectors.
mcqs.explanation: The polygon law generalises the triangle law: by arranging any number of vectors head‑to‑tail to close a polygon, the line joining the start point to the end point gives the resultant. When only three vectors are involved, the polygon reduces to a triangle, which is the triangle law. Option A states this accurately; the other options contain incorrect definitions.

mcqs.question: Two vectors of equal magnitude 10 N act at right angles to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant and its direction relative to the first vector?
mcqs.explanation: When two equal vectors \(F\) are perpendicular, the resultant magnitude is \(F\sqrt{2}\). Here \(10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.14\) N, rounded to 14.1 N. The resultant lies exactly halfway between the two vectors, i.e., at 45° from each. Option B matches both magnitude and direction. The other options are inconsistent with vector addition rules.
